record.issuing_body: The White House (Assistant to the President for Science and Technology; Special Advisor for AI and Crypto; Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs)
record.summary: White House plan of recommended federal policy actions in three pillars: accelerating AI innovation, building AI infrastructure, and leading in international AI diplomacy and security. Its safety and risk content: CAISI to evaluate frontier models for national-security risks such as cyber and CBRNE, and adversary AI systems for backdoors; a DARPA-led programme on interpretability, control and robustness; federal guidelines for AI evaluations; a DHS-led AI-ISAC and AI in incident-response playbooks; requiring federally funded research institutions to use nucleic acid synthesis providers that screen sequences and customers; and a deepfake forensic guideline.
record.notes: Released by the White House on 23 July 2025 under Executive Order 14179 (US-11), which directed the creation of an AI Action Plan; the document itself is dated July 2025. The White House announcement of the release calls it 'Winning the AI Race: America's AI Action Plan' and counts over 90 federal policy actions. The plan is signed by Michael J. Kratsios (Assistant to the President for Science and Technology), David O. Sacks (Special Advisor for AI and Crypto) and Marco A. Rubio (Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs). It says AI-related federal funding should not go to states with burdensome AI regulations, but that the federal government should not interfere with states' rights to pass prudent laws that are not unduly restrictive to innovation, and it asks agencies to consider a state's AI regulatory climate in funding decisions; EO 14365 of December 2025 (US-20) later directed action against state AI laws. It asks NIST to revise the AI RMF (US-02) to remove references to misinformation, diversity, equity and inclusion, and climate change. CAISI's draft NIST AI 800-2 (US-21) answers the plan's call for evaluation guidelines. The White House fact sheet on EO 14434 of 29 September 2026 (US-26) still cites the plan and its more than 90 federal actions.

verification.note: Recheck of 17 Oct 2026: re-read the whitehouse.gov PDF stored on 11 Oct 2026 (the archiver found it unchanged on 17 Oct 2026). It confirms the title, 'JULY 2025', the three signatories and the recommended actions in the summary. The PDF gives only the month; the release day, 23 July 2025, rests on the White House announcement of that day, stored in this run, so date_published stays 2025-07-23. The earlier summary called nucleic acid screening 'mandated'; the plan recommends requiring it. The count of more than 90 federal actions is not in the plan; it comes from the announcement and the White House fact sheet of 29 Sep 2026, both stored in this run, and is now in the notes. The earlier record had eight safety topics; the two least supported ('incident reporting', 'research priorities') were dropped to meet the limit of six. The issuing body now names the signatories by the titles the plan gives them.

judgment.status_reasoning: A non-binding plan of recommended policy actions, released 23 July 2025. Nothing stored withdraws or replaces it; the White House fact sheet of 29 Sep 2026, stored in this run, still cites it. 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: The federal government's AI action plan with substantial safety content (frontier model evaluation for CBRNE and cyber risks, biosecurity screening, AI-ISAC, incident response); in scope with no note.
judgment.date_reasoning: The cover gives 'JULY 2025'; the White House announcement dated 23 July 2025 says the White House 'today released' the plan. date_published 2025-07-23 is therefore confirmed from an official source.

extra_urls.reason: White House article 'White House Unveils America's AI Action Plan', dated 23 July 2025: the release day (date_published 2025-07-23 from an official source instead of the month only) and the plan's 'over 90 Federal policy actions' across three pillars.

White House fact sheet of 29 Sep 2026 on EO 14434 (already stored as US-26's secondary source): says the plan, released in July 2025, identified more than 90 federal actions; supports the notes and shows the plan still cited as current policy.
